title: Regular completed-local comparison above a G-ring quotient
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian semilocal ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $\mathfrak r$ the intersection of its finitely many maximal ideals. Let $J\subseteq\mathfrak r$ be an ideal and suppose that $B/J$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Put $C=\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak r^n$. For every nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ containing $JC$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak Q\cap B$, $U_{\mathfrak p}=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak p}}$ and $T_{\mathfrak Q}=\widehat{C_{\mathfrak Q}}$, where the latter two completions use the respective maximal ideals. Completions are inverse limits of quotients by ideal powers [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and localization at a prime is [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The canonical map $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}:U_{\mathfrak p}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ induced by $B_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a regular local ring homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. No $J$-adic completeness or G-ring hypothesis on $B$ is required.

source.place: Rotthaus (1979), Lemma 4 and Corollaries 4.1–4.2, pp.175–176. This is the regularity of the completed comparison, not regularity of B_p to C_Q. Completeness of the source U_p permits the formally smooth complete-local regularity theorem.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak Q$ as in the statement. Write $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ and $D=C_{\mathfrak Q}$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak QD$. Completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so $C$ is Noetherian. The completion map $B\to C$ is flat. Applying the flat-local-ring-maps lemma to this map and $\mathfrak Q$ gives a flat local homomorphism $f:A\to D$ of Noetherian local rings. Since $JC\subseteq\mathfrak Q$, contraction gives $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$.

Put $E=B/J$ and $H=\varprojlim_n E/(\mathfrak rE)^n$. Apply completion-finite-module-tensor over $B$ to its finite module $E$. Its map $C\otimes_B E\to H$, $c\otimes\bar b\mapsto c\bar b$, is bijective. It preserves products since $(c\bar b)(c^{\prime}\bar b^{\prime})=cc^{\prime}\overline{bb^{\prime}}$ on pure tensors, so it is an isomorphism of rings. The elementary quotient-tensor isomorphism $C\otimes_BE\cong C/JC$, $c\otimes\bar b\mapsto cb\bmod JC$, has inverse $\bar c\mapsto c\otimes1$. Thus $H\cong C/JC$ compatibly with the maps from $E$. The hypothesis that $E$ is a G-ring and the G-ring-completion-regular lemma give regularity of $E\to C/JC$. The target is Noetherian as a quotient of $C$. Put $\bar{\mathfrak Q}=\mathfrak Q/JC$ and $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/J$. Applying regular-local-maximal, implication (1) to (2), gives a regular local map $g:E_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to (C/JC)_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}$.

Apply localization-at-prime-of-quotient to $(B,J,\mathfrak p)$ and $(C,JC,\mathfrak Q)$. It identifies the source and target of $g$ with $A/JA$ and $D/JD$, respectively, by $\overline{b/s}\mapsto\bar b/\bar s$. The maximal ideal of $A/JA$ is $\mathfrak m/JA$ and its residue field is $k=A/\mathfrak m$, by quotient-local-structure. The closed fibre of $g$ is therefore $(D/JD)/(\mathfrak mD/JD)=D/\mathfrak mD$: this equality uses $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$, hence $JD\subseteq\mathfrak mD$. Every map here is induced by $b/s\mapsto b/s$, so this is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras for the original map $f$. Since $g$ is regular, its fibre over the maximal ideal of $A/JA$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$, by the definition of regular ring map. Thus the closed fibre of $f$ is geometrically regular over $k$.

The ring $D/\mathfrak mD$ is a Noetherian local $k$-algebra: $D$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak mD\subseteq\mathfrak n$, so quotient-local-structure applies. Its geometric regularity from Step 3 implies that it is formally smooth over $k$ for its maximal-ideal topology, by geometrically-regular-local-field-adic-smooth. Together with the flatness of $f$ from Step 1, flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic now implies that $D$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

Write $U=\widehat A=U_{\mathfrak p}$ and $T=\widehat D=T_{\mathfrak Q}$. Their maximal ideals are $\mathfrak mU$ and $\mathfrak nT$ and their residue fields are those of $A$ and $D$, by local-completion-local-ring. They are Noetherian by adic-completion-noetherian and complete for these ideals by module-completion-complete, applied to the two finitely generated maximal ideals. Apply fs-adic-complete-source-target to $f$ and Step 4. It gives formal smoothness of the canonical $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}:U\to T$ for $\mathfrak nT$, which is the maximal-ideal topology of $T$. On each quotient coordinate the map sends the class of $a\in A$ to the class of $f(a)\in D$. Consequently $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}$ sends every generator of $\mathfrak mU$ into $\mathfrak nT$ and is local. This is exactly the map specified in the statement, not a chosen comparison isomorphism.

The source and target of $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}$ are complete Noetherian local rings by Step 5. Apply formally-smooth-complete-local-regular to its adic formal smoothness and locality. This proves that $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}$ is regular and in particular flat. A flat local homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat, so flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat proves the final assertion. The only G-ring hypothesis used was on $E=B/J$ in Step 2; no completeness of $B$ was used.
